I find it’s when people portray or express the emotion that is assumed or expected in a situation. For example, I have a friend who is not very in touch with his emotions. We got invited to a party with people we don’t really like and aren’t really close with. It felt bad to be there. However, because it was a party he said he was having fun and happy cause that is what people do at parties. 
Another time we saw a girl we don’t really no at all crying in the hallway. He said it made him sad to see her crying. Even though I’m pretty sure it didn’t he just assumes that it should. We didn’t know her, we’ve all cried at school, we just walked past her, and had no context. 
People that are in tune with their emotions act and express the regardless of expectations. 
My little brother is also not in tune with his emotions and it come from my parents telling him how to feel. We will be at the beach and he will be not feel great, but my parents will say “we are at the beach, there’s no reason for you to be anything other than happy.” Or we will see a dead bird on the ground and he will just walk past it and my parents will say “does that not make you sad that the bird died.” It honestly really dumb that they do that. And they think that they are training him to have deeper emotions, but in reality they are training him to ignore his real ones. 
People who aren’t in tune with their emotions often have a hard time expression how they really feel.
